result: {"findings": [{"file": "examples/cq_two_driver_misuse.zig", "line": 51, "severity": "major", "category": "correctness", "title": "The example leaves four armed Async operations pointing at a dead coroutine frame", "body": "`go` creates `cq` and `mails` on its coroutine stack and submits all four `ev.Async` completions into the queue, but it never tears the queue down. On the path this example is written to detect (no panic), the defers only cancel the two drivers and the feeder. A canceled select deregisters and nothing else: `src/completion_queue.zig:336-339` states it does not close the queue or cancel its operations, and the test at `src/completion_queue.zig:1421` asserts `cq.hasPending()` after exactly that. So `go` returns while up to four Async completions are still armed on the loops, with `c.group.owner` pointing at the dead `cq` and the completions themselves pointing into the freed coroutine stack. A later `ownerCallback` writes to that memory. `std.process.exit(0)` at line 76 also skips the deferred `rt.deinit()`, so the loops are never stopped before the process leaves. The sibling reproducer guards this explicitly (`examples/cq_spurious_select_repro.zig:80-84`, `close(); cancelAll(.keep); drain`). Worse, a crash from that use-after-free is a non-zero exit, which is exactly the signal this example tells a harness to read as \"misuse detected\", so the failure path can report a pass. Add `defer { cq.close(); cq.cancelAll(.keep); while (cq.next()) |_| {} }` right after `cq` is created; registered there it runs last, after both drivers are canceled, so it cannot trip the single-driver check."}, {"file": "examples/cq_two_driver_misuse.zig", "line": 13, "severity": "major", "category": "tests", "title": "The documented death-test harness does not exist, so nothing runs this check", "body": "The header says \"a harness runs it and checks for a NON-zero exit\", but the diff adds no such harness. `build.zig` only adds the example to the `examples` build step, and `check.sh` (the script CI runs, `.github/workflows/test.yml:55`) builds the examples and then executes only `stderr-smoke`. The two-driver panic is therefore compiled but never exercised, on any platform or optimize mode, so a regression that removes the `reg`-slot check in `CompletionQueue.asyncWait` leaves every CI job green. The stated pass criterion is also too weak to use as written: a non-zero exit is produced by any failure, including a spawn error, a `try` propagating out of `main`, or the use-after-free described above. Follow the `stderr-smoke` precedent in `check.sh:153-175`: run the binary, require a non-zero exit, and grep the output for the exact panic text `CompletionQueue: selected from two tasks; one task must drive the queue`."}, {"file": "examples/cq_two_driver_misuse.zig", "line": 70, "severity": "minor", "category": "tests", "title": "The misuse detection is timing-dependent, but exit 0 is declared a hard failure", "body": "The panic fires only when the second driver calls `asyncWait` while the first driver's select is registered, which requires both drivers to be parked at once. `asyncWait` takes the ready fast path without registering whenever `completed` is non-empty, and the feeder re-notifies all four mails continuously, so the queue is ready most of the time. The example acknowledges this (\"Give the two drivers ample time to overlap their parks\") while the header presents the panic as a certainty. Under a loaded or single-core machine, or a qemu-user target, the 5-second window can pass without an overlapping park, and the harness rule in the header turns that into \"MISUSE NOT DETECTED\" — a false failure of a correct implementation. Either drive the two registrations deterministically (park both drivers on an empty queue with the feeder stopped, then release), or state the detection as best-effort so a non-detection is not read as a defect."}, {"file": "src/completion_queue.zig", "line": 1673, "severity": "minor", "category": "tests", "title": "The poison watch uses plain loads, so the optimizer can delete it and Debug pays for 7M byte compares", "body": "The watch loop reads `std.mem.asBytes(&cq)` with ordinary non-atomic, non-volatile loads. The write it is meant to catch would be a data race, which is undefined behaviour, so the compiler is entitled to assume no other thread writes `cq` after `cancelAll` returns and to hoist the loads out of the 500-iteration loop or fold them to the memset constant. CI runs `check.sh --release` (`.github/workflows/test.yml:59`), so in that half of the matrix the instrument can be compiled away entirely and still report a pass, which is the failure mode where a check answers without running. Read the bytes with `@atomicLoad(u8, &b, .monotonic)` (or a volatile pointer) so the reads must be re-issued. In the modes where it is not optimized away the loop is pure cost: 200 rounds x 500 scans x sizeof(CompletionQueue) is roughly 7 million `expectEqual` calls, on top of 200 rounds x 64 long timers submitted from four tasks and canceled, and it never yields, so it also holds an executor thread. The per-backend CI budget is 10 minutes and seven matrix entries run under qemu-user."}]}
